metadata.title: Layered-column vertical scattering and tomographic resolution analysis for L-band radar sounding of sea ice (v2.0)
metadata.description: A horizontally layered snow, sea ice, slush and seawater column is built from field-derived parameters. Brine volume follows Cox and Weeks (1983), brine permittivity Stogryn and Desai (1985), and effective sea-ice permittivity a Polder-van Santen mixture with a single effective depolarization factor constrained simultaneously by accepted cold first-year-ice penetration depths at L-band and C-band. Interface returns follow first-order small-perturbation scattering with an exponential correlation spectrum. Acquisitions are modelled as samples of the vertical wavenumber, verified against exact two-way ray tracing; profiles are estimated by beamforming, Capon and MUSIC, and bounded by a conditional two-reflector Cramer-Rao analysis. A Monte Carlo sub-cell model adds footprint-scale lateral heterogeneity and detector operating characteristics under a deformed-ice confounder.This package extends the semi-empirical forward model archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.19829367. That earlier deposit remains the archive of record for the Commentary and is unchanged by this release. The archival v1.0 module is retained here verbatim, with two documented defects noted in CHANGELOG.md that do not affect the published figure. Requires Python 3.10 or later with numpy, scipy and matplotlib. All random seeds are fixed, so runs are deterministic. MIT licence.

hits.title: Layered-column vertical scattering and tomographic resolution analysis for L-band radar sounding of sea ice (v2.0)

metadata.title: OSCAR-fire
metadata.description:
Overview
OSCAR-fire is an extension of the compact Earth system model OSCAR v3.3. This version uses a bookkeeping scheme with prescribed burned area to assess wildfire carbon fluxes. For the original OSCAR v3 code, visit OSCAR.

Data Dimensions
OSCAR-fire uses the following dimensions for organizing its input and output data:
- year: time axis.
- config: Monte Carlo members, used for uncertainty analysis.
- reg_code: land regions in OSCAR v3.
- bio_land: land biomes; the fire module is applied to Forest and Non-Forest.
- veg_part: vegetation parts (Leaf, Stem, Root).
- pool_part: combustible pools used for combustion completeness and mortality (Leaf, Stem, Root, Litter, CWD).

Drivers
The model requires specific forcing data to run:
- Aburn: burned area during the annual time step (Mha yr-1).
- cveg_0: preindustrial vegetation carbon density (PgC Mha-1).
- D_cveg: change in vegetation carbon density relative to preindustrial (PgC Mha-1).
- csoil_0: preindustrial soil carbon density (PgC Mha-1).
- D_csoil: change in soil carbon density relative to preindustrial (PgC Mha-1).
- veg_frac: fraction of vegetation carbon in Leaf, Stem and Root (1).
- frac_litter: litter fraction of soil carbon (1).
- Aland: biome area (Mha).
- D_tem: land temperature anomaly used for CWD decay (K).

Data Files and Accessibility
The model code is available at GitHub repository. Experiment drivers, parameters and outputs are archived in netCDF format on Zenodo. The output data files represent constrained means and standard deviations from 2,000 configurations.

metadata.title: kpenvelope: self-consistent six-band k.p envelope-function solver for wurtzite heterostructures
metadata.description:
Intersubband optics release: the quantities that turn a solved envelope structure into an absorption spectrum -- and the design numbers of QWIPs and intersubband polaritonic devices.

New in kpenvelope

  • dipole_matrix: the intersubband dipole matrix z_fi = <f|z|i> from any solver's envelopes, all six spinor components summed with the solver's own quadrature, Hermitian by construction.
  • oscillator_strengths: the ground-subband oscillator strengths f_(1->n) = (m*/m0)(E_1 - E_n)|z_1n|^2 / (hbar^2/2m0) in the package's hole convention, normalized so the Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn sum rule reads sum f = 1 for a single parabolic band.

The shipped demo set is six-fold degenerate, so individual matrix elements inside a degenerate multiplet are basis-dependent; the docstrings say plainly that the multiplet-summed quantities are the invariants -- and those are what the anchors pin.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • Infinite-well closed forms on the hard-wall demo set, multiplet-summed: z_12 = 16 L / (9 pi^2) (recovered to 0.7 percent at the tested grid) and f_12 = 256 / (27 pi^2) (recovered to 4 significant figures).
  • The Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn f-sum rule: sum_n f_1n = 1 recovered to a fraction of a percent, with the residual falling as the basis grows.
  • Parity: same-parity transitions on a symmetric well vanish at the 1e-12 level.
  • Gauge: shifting the coordinate origin changes no off-diagonal element -- checked on the coupled six-band Rinke 2008 GaN well, not just the decoupled demo.
  • The dipole matrix is Hermitian by construction and its diagonal sits at the well center.

47 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U kpenvelope.
metadata.notes: If this software is useful in your work, please cite it.

hits.title: kpenvelope: self-consistent six-band k.p envelope-function solver for wurtzite heterostructures

metadata.title: sqzcomb: Lugiato-Lefever steady states and detected squeezing spectra for Kerr microcombs
metadata.description:
Output-entanglement release: the entanglement a detector actually sees lives in the propagating output fields, not in the intracavity state, and the Gaussian toolbox now computes it there.

New in sqzcomb.spectra

  • output_covariance_xxpp: the frequency-resolved covariance matrix of the filtered output quadratures via the input-output relations, in the same xxpp ordering as the intracavity tools.
  • output_entanglement: the logarithmic negativity E_N of any bipartition of the output modes, from the PPT symplectic eigenvalue of that covariance.
  • output_entanglement_spectrum: E_N as a function of analysis frequency -- the curve an experiment traces out by tuning its homodyne detection.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • The output covariance agrees with the package's independent scalar spectrum path element by element (two code paths, one physics, < 1e-13).
  • A passive cavity fed by a thermal input returns an output covariance exactly equal to the thermal value (2 n_B + 1)/2 on the diagonal, and its bipartitions carry exactly zero entanglement.
  • The twin-beam closed form: for the nondegenerate parametric process the output E_N equals -ln(2 V_EPR_min) with the minimal EPR variance computed from the same covariance -- an identity between two independent expressions (< 1e-6).
  • E_N vanishes at zero pump and far from the carrier, and the spectrum decays monotonically away from it on the tested configuration.
  • Detection loss never creates entanglement: E_N after loss <= E_N before, checked across efficiencies.
  • Unstable and invalid inputs are refused rather than silently evaluated.

72 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U sqzcomb.
metadata.notes: If this software is useful in your work, please cite it.

metadata.title: An Agent-Based Platform for the Study of Watersheds as Coupled Natural and Human Systems
metadata.description:
WACCShed:  A Water and Climate Change Watershed Platform

Principal WACCShed Platform Developers: Yu Jie (v1.0), Diego Cardoso (v1.1)
Developers of WACCShed Hydrology Module: David Dziubanski and Kristie Franz
Other Platform Collaborators:  William J. Gutowski, Chris R. Rehmann, and Leigh Tesfatsion
 
WACCShed is an agent-based framework that permits the representation and study of watersheds as dynamic coupled natural and human (CNH) systems. WACCShed permits researchers to undertake systematic computational experiments to explore interactions among hydrology, climate, and human decision-making processes in a watershed over time. A key feature of the platform is its ability to model strategic decision-making among the interacting human participants.
 
The WACCShed Platform  facilitates the balancing of two goals: realism and understanding.  The platform can be used to develop and study a spectrum of watershed models ranging from relatively simple conceptual thought-experiments to detailed empirically-grounded representations. The flexible modular architecture of the platform, developed entirely in Java, eases the transition from one form of modeling to the next.
 
The package included in this deposit is a companion to the published journal article and contains the complete code used to generate the results. Please refer to the README file included in the package for instructions for running simulations in the platform and details about the software architecture. Also, note that the development was concluded in 2017, so dependencies might be outdated and deprecated; please check you are using appropriate versions.

hits.title: An Agent-Based Platform for the Study of Watersheds as Coupled Natural and Human Systems

metadata.title: OrgRec 0.3.2
metadata.description:
OrgRec is a native macOS application for documented pipe-organ field recording. It records multichannel Broadcast Wave audio, retains capture and review evidence, and exports checked research packages.

Version 0.3.2 adds a standalone Analyze Audio workspace: open or drop one audio file, inspect linked waveform, spectrogram, pitch and partial plots, review measurements and signal quality, and export PDF, JSON, CSV, PNG, SVG or a complete folder with the analyzed excerpt, provenance and checksums. No project, catalogue or microphone access is required. Longer recordings use an explicit excerpt, and the original file remains unchanged.

This version supports the published POD 1.6.0 OrgRec SQLite projection through a verified download and offline cache, while retaining the original source identity of supported POD 1.5.0 catalogues. Getting Started guides catalogue installation, local project creation, recording setup and microphone permissions. Spectrum segmentation improvements from 0.3.1 are included. The POD database is distributed separately.

VAO export remains pinned to version 0.5.0, with version-specific historical readers retained. This record contains source from tag v0.3.2 and the universal macOS application, version 0.3.2, build 13, for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later.

The application is ad-hoc signed and is not notarized. Clean-install Finder drag-and-drop and physical capture hardware have not been verified for this release. Unknown-source pitch interpretations remain provisional; audio-file analysis does not supply missing organ, calibration, geometry or collection evidence.

metadata.title: kr-colab/mkado: v0.6.0 - Bug-fix release
metadata.description:
Bug-fix release. No options were added or removed. The thirty fixes below came out of a coverage push that took the test suite from 311 to 718 tests and line coverage from 68 to 95 percent, and out of the bug reports filed along the way. Several fixes change reported numbers: a multi-allelic codon now counts each of its mutations, VCF divergence follows the FASTA rules, pooled polymorphisms filter on the combined minor-allele frequency, and singleton filtering reaches every path. Two fixes remove run-to-run drift: polarized fixed differences no longer follow the hash seed, and separate-files batch pairing no longer follows the directory listing order. Lint and the test suite now run on every pull request.

Fixed

  • In separate-files mode, batch paired an ingroup file with a second outgroup, or with an outgroup found through --outgroup-pattern, by the first _-separated token of its name, taking the first match from an unsorted glob. Gene g1 could take g10's file, and Adh_dmel could take Adh_dsim's, depending on the order the filesystem listed the directory. A partner now has to carry the whole gene name, which is the ingroup stem without its _ingroup or _in marker, followed by _, and candidates are tried in sorted order (closes #117).
  • polarized_mk_test read the second outgroup's codon at a fixed difference with next(iter(set)), so when outgroup2 was polymorphic there the lineage followed Python's hash seed: the same alignment reported the difference on the ingroup lineage, on the outgroup lineage, or as unpolarized from one run to the next. The second outgroup is now read by membership. It names the ancestral codon when it carries exactly one of the two codons, and the difference is unpolarized when it carries both or neither (closes #114).
  • g_test computed its p-value as 1 - cdf, which rounds to exactly zero once the G statistic passes about 75. It now uses the chi-square survival function, so a strongly significant table reports its real p-value instead of zero (closes #35).
  • classify_polymorphism/classify_polymorphism_pooled dropped an entire codon when it had exactly two alleles and the only comparison was stop-blocked, but only dropped the blocked allele when three or more alleles were present. Both now drop just the blocked allele, so classification no longer depends on how many alleles happen to segregate at a codon (closes #94).
  • A codon pair where every mutational ordering passed through a stop codon was dropped from Dn/Ds/Pn/Ps with no signal, indistinguishable from an identical-codon pair. Under the vertebrate mitochondrial code this silently dropped four ordinary Lys/Trp pairs. The pair still drops from the counts, but each drop is now counted and surfaces as a warning, the same way skipped indels and multi-allelic sites already do (closes #90).
  • Asymptotic MK frequency bin edges came from np.linspace, which does not always return the double nearest k / num_bins -- with the default 20 bins, edge 3 came back as 0.15000000000000002 instead of 0.15, misclassifying a polymorphism at exactly that frequency. Bin edges are now computed exactly (closes #84).
  • Pooled-polymorphism frequency filtering was unreliable: polarized_mk_test's pooled branch applied no filter at all, and mk_test's pooled branch filtered on ingroup-only derived counts, missing outgroup-private singletons. Pooled mode now filters on the minor-allele frequency across both groups (closes #83).
  • alpha_tg_from_gene_data reported a zero-width confidence interval for a single gene, or when every bootstrap replicate failed, indistinguishable from a genuinely tight CI. Both cases now report ci_low/ci_high as undefined (NA in pretty/TSV, null in JSON) instead, with batch and vcf emitting a warning (closes #79).
  • --imputed combined with a polarize flag silently ran an unpolarized imputed test instead of erroring, unlike --asymptotic which already rejected the combination (with wording that had itself drifted between test and batch). --plot-asymptotic's ignored-flag warning was missing its "(ignored)" suffix in test. vcf's volcano-plot code caught a broader exception than batch's identical call, swallowing real bugs. --alpha-tg combined with --per-gene silently ignored --per-gene with no warning. The imputed_cutoff and is_aggregate calculations were duplicated verbatim across test/batch/vcf. All six now go through shared helpers (closes #103).
  • test, batch, and vcf each hand-wrote the same option-conflict checks and the copies had drifted: vcf dropped the explanatory clause from its messages, and checked --alpha-tg/--imputed against --asymptotic in a different order than batch, so the same flag combination could report a different conflict depending on the command. All three now share one validator (closes #74).
  • Batch TSV chose its column layout from the first result's type, then silently dropped every row of a different type. A mixed-type batch now raises a clear error instead (closes #69).
  • --output - (a bare dash for stdout) was rejected by the output-path check (closes #46).
  • A failed VCF open leaked one file descriptor; the htslib capture pipe is now closed in every case (closes #45).
  • --no-singletons did not filter singletons on the VCF path; the frequency check let the singleton itself through (closes #40).
  • VCF divergence counting compared the outgroup codon to the reference instead of to the ingroup, miscounting sites where the ingroup was fixed for ALT (closes #44).
  • --freq-cutoffs was not forwarded to per-gene asymptotic workers in vcf mode (closes #42).
  • Batch TSV had no layout for imputed results and silently fell back to JSON (closes #43).
  • Batch JSON silently dropped a gene when two results shared a name; duplicate names are now rejected up front (closes #70).
  • CLI error messages had drifted: some exited without the "Error: " prefix. All CLI errors now route through one helper (closes #72).
  • batch and vcf used different exit codes for an empty result set. Both now exit 0 when a run simply produces no results, and 1 only when genes errored (closes #75).
  • mkado vcf --gene X with -a, --imputed, or --alpha-tg silently ran the standard MK test instead of the requested mode (closes #41).
  • --no-singletons did not filter singletons on the FASTA --polarize-match or --alpha-tg paths, or wherever sample size did not match the raw sequence count. All FASTA paths now filter by derived-allele count, matching the VCF path (closes #55).
  • Pooled major-codon selection weighted each population's frequency spectrum as a proportion, so a small population could outweigh a large one. Sequences are now counted directly (closes #81).
  • Documented how a multi-position codon difference is resolved; the rule was previously unstated (closes #88).
  • A multi-allelic codon collapsed two different derived bases into one mutation. Each base is now counted separately; polymorphism counts rise on affected genes (closes #87).
  • VCF divergence rules now match the FASTA path: a codon touched by an ingroup polymorphism is excluded from divergence, and a heterozygous outgroup call is treated as missing rather than resolved. Divergence counts drop where this applies (closes #58).
  • --freq-cutoffs had no effect on the FASTA per-gene asymptotic fitter; it always used the full frequency range (closes #61).
  • Imputed batch results showed a placeholder adjusted p-value of 1.0 instead of a real Benjamini-Hochberg correction; asymptotic per-gene batches showed a fabricated adjusted-p-value line despite having no p-value (closes #65).
  • A failed curve fit in the asymptotic fitters fell back to a value outside the requested --freq-cutoffs window instead of the last point inside it.
  • format_batch_results accepted an adjusted_pvalues list of the wrong length: a short list raised an IndexError from inside a format branch and a long list was silently truncated. It now raises a ValueError before formatting anything (#116).

metadata.title: music: extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements
metadata.description:
Extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements, based on the MASS framework: psychophysical descriptions of musical elements in LPCM audio, expressed as equations and corresponding Python routines. State is updated at every sample, so a rendered sound is as close as it can be to the mathematical model that describes it.

The package covers synthesis of notes and their variation (vibrato, glissando, FM and AM, ADSR envelopes, the six noise colours), filters and their design, spatialisation by interaural time and intensity difference and by measured head-related transfer functions, reverberation, music theory (the diatonic modes, the minor scales, triads and tetrads, the intervals and their names, the harmonic series), permutation groups and change-ringing peals, and a sensory-stimulation toolkit whose stimuli each name the technique they implement in the SSTIM vocabulary.

Its correspondence with the published framework is measured rather than asserted. Every routine is compared with the MASS reference implementation, and separately against the numbered equations of the article itself: 26 of the reference's 35 routines are reproduced sample for sample and the rest diverge for stated reasons, and 45 of the article's 47 labelled equations are checked by a test, which is all of those a test could settle. Where the article, the reference implementation and this package disagree, the disagreement is recorded with the evidence for it.

metadata.title: vcjdeboer/nanodrop-pylabrobot-demo: v1.0.0 — NanoDrop 1000 via PyLabRobot
metadata.description:
First archived release: a legacy Thermo Scientific NanoDrop ND-1000 driven entirely through PyLabRobot on macOS, measuring a real UV absorbance spectrum of paracetamol (acetaminophen).

Contents:

  • Raw measurement data (10x-averaged blank + paracetamol absorbance arrays)
  • Plots: blank reference, single vs 10x averaging, boxcar vs Savitzky-Golay smoothing, final spectrum
  • README documenting the measurement pipeline and results
  • Two hardware-verified macOS fixes to the ND-1000 driver (tolerant clear_halt; USB reset for reliable lamp-off)

Built on Jordvl's open-science ND1000 reverse-engineering and PyLabRobot PR #1166.
